playbook:
- When asked to file a claim, I always file the true result the office gave me. The rules require the claim to match the private result, and honest claims also make me a trustworthy partner for escort coordination.
- When the hiding decision is put to me, I avoid the obvious middle (5) and rotate among less-salient cells like 2, 3, 7, 8 so standing-order shots are less likely to land. Reusing cell 7 worked this game and I never got hit, but that was partly luck; rotation among 2-4 cells remains my default. I only repeat a cell if I have a specific read that my chaser avoids it, and after several rounds at one cell (as I did with 7) I shift off it before devotion turns into a pattern someone can exploit — my late switch to 8 was the right instinct.
- When the fire decision is put to me, I fire on my assigned standing-order target unless there is a clear, mutually agreed reason not to — the rotation keeps damage distributed and avoids provoking retaliation. I vary my firing cells based on the shot log rather than fixing on one number: firing 7 every round hit once early then whiffed repeatedly, so I rotate my aim across the target's plausible cells, favouring ones they favoured two or more rounds ago and the cell I last saw them shot at without being hit.
- When considering firing on Harbor for the payroll transfer: I do it only if I am behind late and the +3/-3 swing exceeds the cost of being put off the board. While tied or ahead, or while my escort engine is running, I leave Harbor alone — a working mutual escort already outearns the raid with none of the risk. I treat Harbor's threat as credible; this game Harbor sat at -3 and nobody profited from raiding it.
- When the note stage comes, I use notes actively in round 1 to build the escort pair: propose "I escort X if X escorts me", name the specific boat, and invite confirmation by note, since a mutual escort pays +5 each — far more than any shot. My round-1 proposal to Foxtrot set up the entire game. Once the pair is locked, a quiet "steady on station" is fine mid-game, but I return to explicit renewal in the final round (naming my partner and intent, as I did in round 6) to protect against last-round defection, and I go straight back to explicit proposals the moment anything wobbles.
- When the escort decision is put to me, I name the boat that publicly agreed to name me, and I name it even on the final round — the payout doesn't depend on future rounds, and final-round defection buys little since the office pays on naming, not on future trust. I never answer "none" if any boat has signalled it will name me. The Echo–Foxtrot mutual paying +5 every single round was the entire engine of my +34 finish; protecting that pairing is my top priority in every round.
- If an escort partner defects (I name them, they don't name me), I name someone else next round or none, and I say so in my note so the defector is identified. If they publicly return to cooperation, I restore the pairing rather than abandoning +5 a round out of spite — one early defection is forgivable if the engine restarts.
- When points are tied or I lead narrowly late, I prioritize the guaranteed escort +5 over trying to break ahead via hits: a coordinated mutual escort in the last rounds is the highest-EV move available, so I spend my notes locking it in rather than deceiving about shots.
- Overall, the plan that scored +34 — honest claims, standing-order fire, rotating hides and aims, and a rock-solid mutual escort every single round — is my default from round 1 next time. I only deviate (Harbor raid, firing off-rotation) if the escort engine collapses or I fall clearly behind with rounds running out.

1.text:
- When the rules say my claim must match the private result the office gives me, I always claim truthfully. A false claim is either rejected or marks me as a liar to the whole picket, and it earns nothing.

- The mutual escort payout (5 points each) dwarfs a hit (4 points) and is the biggest scoring lever in the game. From round 1 I use my station note to openly propose a pairing with one named boat — e.g. "Foxtrot escorts Echo; Echo, name me back" — and then I actually file that boat at the escort stage every round until it reciprocates. Persistence paid off: Echo and I locked in and banked 5 points every round.

- Once a partner reciprocates, I stay loyal for the whole patrol. Switching partners mid-game risks breaking the mutual and getting nothing; a stable pairing compounds 5 points every round.

- When my proposed partner does not reciprocate within one or two rounds, I pivot my note and escort claim to the other boat rather than filing "none". Filing "none" while others pair up is how I finish behind; I never do that.

- In the final round I still post an explicit note naming my escort partner so the mutual is confirmed even if earlier notes went bland or unacknowledged; a pairing only pays if both boats file it, so I make the confirmation unmistakable.

- I keep my escort partner out of my line of fire where the standing order allows, and I say so in notes, so the pairing survives the shooting.

- I never fire on Harbor unless 3 points swings the game for me in the final round; the jettison tax plus Harbor's retaliation threat makes it bad value otherwise. Someone hit Harbor for -3 anyway, which confirms the threat is not empty.

- My full-patrol shooting record was all misses despite rotating cells, so I revise the firing plan: I track every shot at each of my targets and systematically sweep the line so no cell gets tried twice at an evasive target, treating it as a coverage problem over 6 rounds rather than a guessing game. If a target shows a habit (e.g. hiding near its own recent fire cell or favoring the middle), I exploit it directly; if nothing is working, I fire the center cells in late rounds since rotating edges found nobody.

- When hiding, I avoid repeating my own previous cell and avoid the cells where I have been shooting others — targets sometimes mirror. If an opponent has just hit me, I move to the opposite end of the line from where I was found. When nobody is allowed to fire on me (I am not the standing target that round and nobody broke the order all game), I can safely recycle a cell the shooter has already fired and missed.

- When I am the standing target that round, I change cell every round and favor cells far from where I was last shot at. In this episode Echo missed me every round at 7, 9, and elsewhere — unpredictable movement worked; I keep doing it.

- In notes I stay otherwise bland and steady unless I am negotiating an escort; notes are free and the only channel for arranging the 5-point mutual, so every note either proposes or confirms a pairing.

- In the final round I check the score standings first: if shooting is the only path to first place, I fire at the leader rather than mechanically following the standing order, since nothing punishes deviating and a 4-point hit can flip a tied or near-tied finish. I tied Echo at 29 this episode — next time, if the final-round margin is within one hit, I defect from the order and shoot the boat I'm racing.

2.text:
When the claim stage comes, I always file the claim that matches the private result exactly — the rules require it and there is no bluff option. I did this every round and it held up; never deviate.

Escort is the engine of this game and pairing decided everything again: Echo (29) and Foxtrot (24) locked onto each other round 1 and collected 5 every round while I scored 3 total. My critical failure this time: I proposed to Echo in round 1, then kept naming Echo for five straight rounds even though Echo never named me back — I never executed my own pivot rule. So the rule is now strict and mechanical: round 1, make an explicit exclusive offer to ONE boat in my note ("I name you every round, name me back") and name them at the escort stage. The moment one escort result comes back without reciprocation, I switch my offer AND my escort claim to the third boat the very next round — no second chances, no hoping. If that also fails (the other two are already paired with each other), I stop spending escort claims on the pair entirely.

When choosing between the two boats for my initial offer, prefer whichever looks less likely to pair with the other — but honestly the round-1 choice is a coin flip, which is exactly why the instant pivot matters more than the pick.

If I'm locked out as the outsider, I switch fully to salary mode: fire on Harbor every remaining round for the guaranteed 3. I did this in rounds 5-6 and it produced my entire score (+3); I should have started the moment my round-1 offer wasn't reciprocated, not midway. A 1-of-9 standing-order shot at another boat is a bad bet — again this game, every standing-order shot missed for five straight rounds — so escort income and Harbor salary are the only reliable points, and if I can't have the first I take the second immediately.

On Harbor's retaliation threat: Harbor finished at -3 and never put anyone off the board despite my round 5-6 shots and my publicly announced round-6 defection. So the threat was cheap talk here. My policy: watch whether Harbor actually punishes the first defector (anyone, not just me). If round 2 starts with no punishment after a Harbor shot, fire on Harbor every round from then on. If I have a live escort pairing and Harbor does punish, comply with standing orders until the final round. The final round is always a free Harbor shot regardless — retaliation can't reach it.

When I do fire a standing-order shot at a boat (only while protecting a live escort deal and Harbor's goodwill), I track the target's hide history and shoot repeated cells; otherwise center cells 4-6. I always expect a miss and never plan around the +4.

When hiding: Foxtrot shot at me all game again. Rotate every round, never repeat a recent cell, default to edge/off-center cells (1-2, 8-9) since shooters gravitate center, and never say anything about location in notes.

Notes: my only negotiation channel, visible to Harbor too. Round 1 note = explicit escort offer. Round 2+ = either confirmation, a new offer to the third boat, or a public callout of non-reciprocators to apply pressure. Announcing my final-round Harbor shot cost nothing, but there's no upside either — I'll keep notes relevant to escort or say "steady on station" and not tip shots before the last round is locked.

Per-round priority: (1) get or keep a mutual escort — pivot partners instantly on non-reciprocation; (2) if locked out, fire on Harbor from that round onward for the guaranteed 3; (3) if paired, follow standing orders unless Harbor's threat proves empty; (4) final round, always fire Harbor; (5) never file a claim that contradicts the private result; (6) never hide predictably.
